models.citation: AlleleForge contributors (heuristic); mechanism after Marquart et al. 2021 (BE-DICT)
models.intended_use: A deterministic, dependency-free default base-editing window-outcome prior (which editable bases are edited and the bystander spectrum). For the published BE-DICT outcome use the opt-in trained model (be-dict). Research use.
known_failure_modes: Transparent motif heuristic, not the trained BE-DICT model: a re-run from this checkpoint reproduces the heuristic, not published BE-DICT numbers. Use be-dict for the trained model.
Treats editable positions as independent and does not model deaminase- and context-dependent bystander transfer.
models.name: be-dict-baseline
models.out_of_scope_use: Trusting the outcome as the trained BE-DICT prediction (it is a transparent heuristic); clinical decision-making; chemistries other than base editing.

models.citation: AlleleForge contributors (heuristic); mechanism after Mathis et al. 2023/2024 (PRIDICT2.0)
models.intended_use: A deterministic, dependency-free default that exercises the calibrated- uncertainty and OOD plumbing end to end and gives a reasonable geometry-based ranking prior. For published PRIDICT2.0 efficiency use the opt-in trained model (pridict2). Research use.
known_failure_modes: Transparent geometry heuristic, not the trained PRIDICT2.0 model (method=HEURISTIC): a re-run from this checkpoint reproduces the heuristic, not published PRIDICT2.0 numbers. Use pridict2 for the trained model.
Cell-context OOD is flagged from the HEK293T/K562 window, but the score itself does not model chromatin without ePRIDICT + an ENCODE track.

No edit-size or edit-class feature: two pegRNAs with identical geometry score identically whether they write one base or a 29-nt insertion, which the RTT-length penalty only indirectly proxies. A score for a non-single-base edit carries an explicit note saying so; use the trained pridict2 model for size-aware numbers.
models.name: pridict2-baseline
models.out_of_scope_use: Trusting the point estimate as the trained PRIDICT2.0 prediction (it is a transparent heuristic); clinical decision-making; a substitute for experimental validation.

models.citation: AlleleForge contributors (heuristic); byproduct channels after Anzalone et al. 2019 (prime editing)
models.intended_use: A deterministic, dependency-free default for the intended-vs-byproduct distribution and the intended probability that feeds the menu's cleanliness objective. Research use.
known_failure_modes: Transparent geometry heuristic, not a trained byproduct model: a re-run from this checkpoint reproduces the heuristic, not measured product distributions.

Keyed on pegRNA geometry only — no target-sequence context, no cell type, and no edit-size or edit-class term, so two pegRNAs with identical geometry receive the same split whether they write one base or a 29-nt insertion.
The three modeled byproduct channels (scaffold incorporation, partial RT product, indel) are the dominant ones, not an exhaustive account of what a pegRNA can produce.
models.name: prime-outcome-baseline
models.out_of_scope_use: Trusting the byproduct split as a measured product distribution (it is a transparent heuristic); clinical decision-making; a substitute for sequencing the edited product.

body.rationale:
Routing: base_abe=yes, base_cbe=no, prime=yes, cas9_nuclease=no.
Eligible and run: base_abe, prime.
Why the other chemistries declined:
- base_cbe: Cytosine base editing installs a C->T / G->A transition in a narrow window with no double-strand break — eligible when the required change is a G:C->A:T transition SNV.
- cas9_nuclease: An SpCas9 double-strand break repaired by error-prone NHEJ yields frameshifting indels that ablate gene function — the canonical knock-out route.
- ClinVar: pathogenic
- intent install writes an allele ClinVar classifies as pathogenic — a disease model, not a correction
- base_abe: 1 candidate(s)
- prime: eligible but no actionable candidate enumerated — no PAM match at this offset (155); the spacer contains TTTT, which terminates Pol III transcription (1)
Ranked by a weighted sum of four higher-is-better objectives (efficiency 0.35, cleanliness 0.30, safety 0.30, simplicity 0.05); the safety term uses the worst-affected ancestry and the efficiency term is uncertainty-discounted. The Pareto front lists the 1 candidate(s) not dominated on all four objectives.
